The test image shows two corn ears on the stalk. The lower ear has a large dark brown gall/mass where kernels should be, with husks pulled back. The upper ear looks relatively normal with orange kernels. This dark mass replacing ear tissue is highly suggestive of smut.

Let me check a Common Smut reference.

The reference image shows Classic Common Smut: white-to-silvery galls on the ear that turn dark/black with spore masses. The test image shows a large dark brown gall mass replacing part of the ear — this is a later-stage Common Smut gall where the spore mass has matured and darkened. The adjacent ear on the same plant appears normal, which is consistent with Common Smut (can infect individual plant parts while others remain unaffected).
